summary.en: Venezuela is reeling from deadly earthquakes that have killed thousands and triggered a humanitarian response, while President Nicolás Maduro and his wife have pleaded not guilty to U.S. torture conspiracy charges and face a trial delayed until 2027. The United States has lifted sanctions on the leader of Venezuela's National Assembly and has deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela, mirroring actions taken in Iran. Chile has sentenced a Venezuelan gang member to 20 years for kidnapping and killing a dissident. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Venezuela vakler etter dødelige jordskjelv som har drept tusenvis og utløst en humanitær respons, mens president Nicolás Maduro og hans kone har erklært seg uskyldige i amerikanske tortur-konspirasjonsanklager og står overfor en rettssak som er utsatt til 2027. USA har opphevet sanksjoner mot lederen av Venezuelas nasjonalforsamling og har satt i drift elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer fra Space Force mot Venezuela, i likhet med tiltak som ble iverksatt mot Iran. Chile har dømt et venezuelansk gjengmedlem til 20 år for kidnapping og drap på en dissident. To dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
